translations.translation: "She who dwells in the gardens, etc., my Beloved has fled, etc., upon the mountains of spices"1,
and the Admor
(the Horav Shalom Ber)
of blessed memory explains in his maamar beginning with these words2
which he said on 24 Tevet3
(the day of the yahrzeit of the Alter Rebbe),
that "she who dwells in the gardens" speaks of the revelation of the Garden of Eden4,
"gardens"
(in the plural)
are5
the lower Garden of Eden and the upper Garden of Eden, which are in Beriah, Yetzirah, and Asiyah
(the lower Garden of Eden is in Asiyah, and the upper Garden of Eden is in Beriah6),
and "she who dwells in the gardens" means7
Malchut of Atzilut, which contracts itself to dwell in the gardens,
and "my Beloved has fled, etc., upon the mountains of spices" speaks of the revelation of the future,
which is vastly superior, even beyond comparison, to the revelation of the Garden of Eden,
for the revelation of the Garden of Eden is the immanent light, and the revelation of the future is the encompassing light.
For this is the meaning of "fled, etc., upon the mountains of spices"
(specifically "fled"),
that the ascent from the revelation of the Garden of Eden to the revelation of the future is by way of flight and leap, not in order and gradation.
Nevertheless,
in order to receive the revelation of the encompassing light of the future,
it is specifically through the prior revelation of the immanent light of the Garden of Eden.
And this is "she who dwells in the gardens"
(and afterwards)
"my Beloved has fled, etc., upon the mountains of spices",
that first there must be the revelation of "she who dwells in the gardens," and through this specifically one arrives
(by way of flight and leap)
at the revelation of "the mountains of spices."

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the difference between immanent and encompassing light, arguing that the immanent light inherently has a relationship to division, as proven by the fact that the encompassing light is not affected by vessels.

translations.translation: And the explanation of the matter:
The difference between immanent light and encompassing light is,
that encompassing light is simple light,
while immanent light comes in division,
the light of wisdom, the light of kindness, etc.
And it is explained in the aforementioned maamar,
that from the fact that immanent light comes in division,
even though the actual division is caused by its being clothed in the vessels,
it is necessary to say,
that also in the light itself
(before its clothing in vessels)
there is a relationship to division.
For in the Pardes8
it is explained,
that the division that occurs in the light through its clothing in vessels,
is only with regard to its activity
(in what manner it acts upon the creations,
for when it is clothed in the vessel of kindness, it performs the activity of kindness,
and so on with all the Sefiros),
but the light itself remains in its simplicity.
And based on this, one could say,
that the light, in and of itself
(before its clothing in vessels)
is completely simple
(that it has no relationship to division at all),
like the analogy of sunlight
(brought in the Pardes8),
that although in itself it is simple light
(for light is of the same kind as the luminary and is attached to the luminary),
nevertheless, when it shines through a white, red, or green glass,
it appears
(and acts)
according to the color of the vessel.
However, at first glance, this explanation is insufficient9.
For it is known10,
that encompassing light,
even when it shines within the vessels,
the vessel does not effect a change in it,
not even that it should appear according to the manner of the vessel
[and as is also brought in the aforementioned maamar,
that the light of Atik11,
even as it is drawn into Zeir Anpin,
is in the category of simplicity].
And from this it is proven10,
that this, that in immanent light there occurs
(through the vessels)
a form and division
(with regard to its activity, at least)
is because this light
(even before its clothing in vessels)
is of the category of division.
